tasks.short: Look at costs, revenue and commitments in AFAS and project next quarters for the forecast and advice.

today.trigger: Quarterly forecast round, a request from the Finance Director or FP&A, or a large new contract or lease.
steps: Export ledger, open orders and commitments from AFAS to Excel
Pull flex worker hours and agency invoice totals from the three agency portals
Adjust last year's run rate for known changes (CAO raises, new customers, fuel)
Build or update the projection workbook per site
Write a short note on drivers and risks for the Controller
drudgery: Re-exporting and re-mapping the same AFAS reports each quarter
Keying agency hours into Excel by hand
today.time_sinks: Collecting and reconciling data from AFAS and three agency portals before any analysis starts; chasing site managers for known changes.

lenses.faster: A driver model fed nightly from the AFAS extract and agency hours removes the export and re-mapping steps; the accountant starts from a ready baseline.
lenses.autonomous: Each month after close the baseline projection refreshes and flags drivers that moved more than a set threshold.
lenses.ambitious: A rolling 18-month projection per site and per customer, including flex labour by season, instead of a quarterly spreadsheet.
lenses.joy: No more copying exports; the time goes to asking site managers what is really changing.
lenses.options: Base, low-volume and high-wage-settlement scenarios produced side by side, each with its assumptions listed.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the driver definitions and checks the model's back-test each quarter rather than building the workbook.
reach: FP&A Analyst: first-pass rolling forecast per site
Controller: commitment and obligations overview for the board pack

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which customer is about to leave, what the next CAO round will likely cost and which assumption the business will not believe.
tasks.pattern_why: Several sources and steps with exceptions (missing agency data, one-off items); a person must approve the assumptions before numbers go to the Finance Director.

in_practice.trigger: Month close completed in AFAS, or a forecast round opened by FP&A.
steps: Load actuals, open orders and commitments from the nightly AFAS extract
Load agency hours and invoices per site
Run the driver model and back-test against last quarter
Draft a projection with listed assumptions and a variance note
Accountant reviews, edits assumptions and approves
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves assumptions and figures before they go to FP&A or the Finance Director.
data_needed: General ledger actuals by site and cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint forecast folder with versioned assumptions sheet and approval note

evidence.claim: Accountants using AI closed the month 7.5 days faster across 79 firms.
evidence.source: CFO Dive on Choi and Xie study, 13 Aug 2025 [S3]

evidence.claim: Multi-step reasoning across files is the main failure mode of current models on accounting tasks.
A driver model on a nightly ERP extract can produce a baseline projection without a model in the loop.

risks: A model adds an unstated assumption and the projection cannot be rebuilt
Agency portal data arrives late or in changing formats
Business stops trusting the forecast if one scenario is wildly off
research_questions: How far off were the last four manual projections, and would a simple driver model have beaten them?
Can the three agency portals deliver hours and invoices in a stable export or API?
Which assumptions does the Finance Director actually challenge each quarter?

tasks.short: Check transactions and processes for weak controls, duplicates, waste, fraud or rule breaches.

today.trigger: Year-end audit preparation, an auditor's management letter, or a suspicious payment spotted by a bookkeeper.
steps: Export AP, vendor master and payment batches from AFAS and Rabobank
Sample invoices and payments in Excel
Check for duplicate invoices, changed IBANs and approvals by the wrong person
Compare agency invoices with ordered hours
Write findings for the Controller
drudgery: Sampling by hand when the full population could be checked
Matching agency invoices to hours line by line
today.time_sinks: Exporting and cleaning data, and following up every false hit in a sample.

lenses.faster: Rule-based tests run over every transaction, so sampling and manual matching disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Tests run nightly on the AFAS extract and each payment batch before release, and open an exception item only on a hit.
lenses.ambitious: Full-population checks on every payment, vendor change and agency invoice, instead of a sample once a year.
lenses.joy: No more scrolling through exports; the accountant investigates real exceptions.
lenses.options: Several thresholds per test can be tried on last year's data to pick the one with the fewest false hits.
lenses.altitude: The accountant designs, tunes and documents the test library and reviews its hit rate with the auditor.
reach: Bookkeeper: duplicate-invoice and IBAN-change checks before payment
Controller: continuous evidence for the internal control framework

tasks.human_edge: Judging intent, talking to the people involved and deciding when a pattern is fraud, sloppiness or a legitimate exception.
tasks.pattern_why: Duplicates, segregation-of-duties conflicts, IBAN changes and hours-versus-invoice mismatches are rules over structured data with checkable output.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract load and each Rabobank payment batch before approval.
steps: Run duplicate, IBAN-change, segregation-of-duties and approval-limit tests
Match agency invoices to ordered and registered hours
Score and queue exceptions
LLM step drafts a finding text per confirmed exception
Accountant investigates and closes or escalates
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant decides every escalation; interviews and fraud follow-up stay with people.
in_practice.logs_to: Exception register in SharePoint with test version, hit, decision and reviewer

evidence.claim: Full-population tests for duplicates, segregation of duties and IBAN changes fit deterministic software at autonomy 4.
Agents prepare work but teams stay responsible for review.

risks: Too many false hits and people stop looking
Access to HR and payroll data for tests must respect AVG/GDPR purpose limits
Monitoring employees' approval behaviour may need works council (OR) consent under WOR art. 27
research_questions: How many duplicate payments or IBAN changes were found in the last two years, and how?
Does the AFAS extract include the vendor master change log and user approval log?
Will the external auditor rely on the test library, reducing their own sampling?

tasks.short: Maintain budgets and make the monthly budget-versus-actual reports per site and cost centre.

today.trigger: Month close, and the annual budget round in autumn.
steps: Load the budget into AFAS or Excel
Export actuals after close
Map accounts to budget lines and calculate variances
Ask cost centre owners to explain large variances
Write commentary and send the report
drudgery: Rebuilding the same variance tables every month
today.time_sinks: Mapping and reconciling actuals to budget lines and collecting explanations from site managers.

lenses.faster: The Power BI report computes variances from the nightly extract; an LLM drafts commentary from the numbers and owners' notes.
lenses.autonomous: After close the report builds itself and sends each owner their variances above threshold with a short form to explain.
lenses.ambitious: Weekly flash reports per site and per customer, including flex labour, instead of one monthly pack.
lenses.joy: No more table-building; the accountant talks with owners about why costs moved.
lenses.options: Budget re-forecast options (hold, reallocate, cut) drafted for each big variance.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains the account mapping, thresholds and commentary rules and checks the output.
reach: Controller: budget round templates and owner follow-up

tasks.human_edge: Pressing owners on explanations that do not add up and deciding what to tell the Finance Director.
tasks.pattern_why: Variance calculations are rules over structured data; only the commentary needs an LLM step with a tie-out check.

steps: Refresh actuals and budget in Power BI
Compute variances and flag those above threshold
Send owners a Teams form for explanations
LLM drafts commentary tied to the figures
Accountant reviews and releases the pack
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves commentary and figures before release.
data_needed: Budget by cost centre and month
in_practice.logs_to: Monthly report folder in SharePoint with tie-out sheet and approval

evidence.claim: Management reports, budget against actual: deterministic software plus LLM commentary at autonomy 3.
AI-assisted close was 7.5 days faster in a field study.

risks: Commentary states a cause that the owner never gave
Mapping errors flow silently into every report
research_questions: How many hours per month go into the current variance pack?
Do owners answer a structured Teams form faster than mail?
Is the nightly extract complete enough on the day after close?

tasks.short: Check payroll and personnel data for correct wage tax, WW, WIA and Zvw premiums and liabilities.

today.trigger: Monthly payroll tax return, year-end, a Belastingdienst query or the auditor's payroll work.
steps: Export payroll journals and employee contract data from AFAS
Check contract types against high/low WW premium rules
Reconcile payroll liabilities with the general ledger
Check flex workers' agency invoices for correct rates and hours
Note issues for the Payroll Specialist
drudgery: Checking contract type and premium rate employee by employee
Matching payroll journals to ledger accounts
today.time_sinks: Reconciling payroll journals to the ledger and checking WW premium classification across 1,200 employees and changing contracts.

lenses.faster: Rule checks on every employee record replace sampling: contract type versus WW rate, Zvw caps, sector fund, and journal-to-ledger tie-out.
lenses.autonomous: Each payroll run triggers the checks before the wage tax return is filed and flags mismatches.
lenses.ambitious: Every payroll run fully checked, including flex worker cost against agency agreements and CAO scales.
lenses.joy: No line-by-line checking; the accountant works with Payroll on the few real issues.
lenses.options: Scenarios for liabilities (sickness under eigenrisicodragerschap, WGA) at different absence levels.
lenses.altitude: The accountant writes and maintains the payroll control rules with the Payroll Specialist and reviews hit rates.
reach: Payroll Specialist: pre-filing checks on the wage tax return
HR Administrator: contract data quality checks

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting unclear cases (oproepkrachten, contract changes mid-month) and agreeing corrections with Payroll and the tax office.
tasks.pattern_why: Premium rules and tie-outs are written-down rules on structured AFAS data with checkable results.

in_practice.trigger: Payroll run finalised in AFAS, before the loonaangifte is submitted.
steps: Pull payroll journal and contract data for the run
Run premium, cap and contract-type rules
Tie payroll liabilities to the general ledger
Queue exceptions to Payroll with the rule that fired
Accountant reviews exceptions and signs off
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant and Payroll Specialist approve corrections before filing.
in_practice.logs_to: Payroll control log in SharePoint per run, with exceptions and sign-off

evidence.claim: Internal control and payroll checks fit deterministic tests over every transaction.
No benchmark covers Dutch payroll or premium rules.

risks: Rules go stale when premium rates or laws change each January
Payroll data is personal data; access must be limited under AVG/GDPR
Wrong WW classification at scale creates back-payments
research_questions: How many premium or classification errors did the last audit or tax inspection find?
Does AFAS hold contract type data reliably enough to test the WW rule?
Who will own updating the rules each January?

tasks.short: Advise managers and HR on cost of pay, benefits, finance system design and tax planning.

today.trigger: A question from HR, the Finance Director or a site manager, such as cost of a CAO change or a new pension or lease scheme.
steps: Clarify the question with the requester
Gather payroll, CAO and ledger data
Calculate costs or tax effects in Excel
Write an advice note or slides
Discuss in a meeting
drudgery: Rebuilding cost calculations from scratch per question
Looking up rules and CAO texts
today.time_sinks: Gathering data and checking rules before the actual advice can be written.

lenses.faster: A copilot drafts the cost model and a first advice note from AFAS data and the CAO text on SharePoint.
lenses.autonomous: Little runs alone; the copilot can prepare a briefing when a new CAO or tax rule is published.
lenses.ambitious: Every HR and benefits proposal gets a costed, tax-checked note before it goes to the works council.
lenses.joy: Less looking up; more time talking with HR about what the scheme should achieve.
lenses.options: Three to five scheme variants with cost, tax and cash effects side by side.
lenses.altitude: The accountant keeps reusable cost models and checklists that the copilot fills.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: costing of benefit changes
HR Business Partner: cost of restructuring options

tasks.human_edge: Understanding what the requester really needs, weighing works council and employee reactions, and taking responsibility for the advice.
tasks.pattern_why: Advice depends on context, trust and liability; AI speeds up drafting and options but the person leads.

in_practice.trigger: Advice request logged by HR, Finance Director or a site manager.
steps: Accountant states the question and constraints
Copilot gathers data and drafts cost model and options
Accountant checks numbers and rules, adjusts
Copilot drafts the advice note
Accountant presents and discusses
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant owns and signs the advice; tax positions reviewed by the Controller or adviser.
in_practice.logs_to: Advice register in SharePoint with versions and sources

evidence.claim: Client communication and asking the right questions were left out of the benchmark where AI beat CPAs.
Tax estimates belong on the mandatory human review list.

risks: Payroll data in a general AI tool breaks AVG/GDPR rules
research_questions: How many advice requests a year does the accountant handle, and how long does each take?
Which data may legally be used in the copilot under the company's AVG/GDPR policy?
Do requesters value options or a single clear recommendation?

tasks.short: Check new or changed systems (AFAS setup, e-invoicing, interfaces) will work correctly before go-live.

today.trigger: An AFAS upgrade or configuration change, a new interface (bank, agency portal), or e-invoicing preparation.
steps: Read the design or change description
Write test cases for postings, VAT codes and approvals
Run tests in the test environment
Compare results with expected ledger outcomes
Sign off or list issues for IT and the Controller
today.time_sinks: Designing test cases and checking outcomes line by line.

lenses.faster: A copilot drafts test cases from the change description and a script compares test postings with expected results.
lenses.autonomous: Regression tests on postings and VAT codes rerun after every AFAS update.
lenses.ambitious: A standing regression pack for every finance flow, ready for the e-invoicing obligation from 2030.
lenses.joy: Less hand-checking; more time on design questions.
lenses.options: Several test sets (normal, edge, fraud attempts) generated for each change.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the finance control requirements and the regression pack, not each test run.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: tests for AFAS HR-to-finance postings

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether the design fits how the business really works and whether controls are strong enough.
tasks.pattern_why: The person decides what to test and whether the system is fit; AI drafts tests and compares outputs.

in_practice.trigger: Change request or AFAS release note for a finance-relevant change.
steps: Copilot drafts test cases from the change description
Accountant reviews and adds edge cases
Script runs tests and compares postings to expected
Accountant reviews differences and signs off or rejects
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant signs the go-live decision with the Controller.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and VAT codes
in_practice.logs_to: Test log and sign-off in SharePoint per change

evidence.claim: Dutch B2B e-invoicing is planned from 1 July 2030, not yet law.
AI can draft test cases from a change description.

risks: Generated tests miss the edge case that matters
Test data copied from production contains personal data
research_questions: How many finance-relevant system changes happen per year?
Does AFAS offer a test environment fit for automated regression tests?
What did the last go-live problems cost in corrections?

tasks.short: Report audit findings and asset use to management and propose changes.

today.trigger: After the year-end audit, an internal review, or a quarterly asset review (trucks, forklifts, warehouse equipment).
steps: Collect findings and asset data from AFAS fixed assets
Calculate use and cost per asset or site
Write a report with recommendations
Discuss with the Controller and Finance Director
Track agreed actions
drudgery: Rewriting findings into a management format
today.time_sinks: Pulling asset and finding data together and writing the report.

lenses.faster: An LLM drafts the report from the exception register and asset data; the accountant edits.
lenses.autonomous: Action tracking reminds owners and updates status without the accountant chasing.
lenses.ambitious: Quarterly asset use reviews per site, linking idle equipment to lease and purchase decisions.
lenses.joy: Less formatting and chasing; more discussion of what to change.
lenses.options: Several recommendation sets with cost and effect for management to choose from.
lenses.altitude: The accountant designs the reporting template and finding standards and checks the drafts.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what to escalate, how to say it, and persuading managers to act.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured findings and asset data go in; a draft report with traceable figures comes out inside a fixed workflow.

steps: Pull exceptions and asset data
LLM drafts report with figures tied to sources
Accountant edits and sets recommendations
Present to management and log actions
Automatic reminders track actions
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves the report and recommendations before release.
data_needed: Fixed asset register and use data
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint report folder and action tracker

evidence.claim: LLM-written findings at autonomy 3 on top of deterministic tests.
A model can add an unnoticed assumption so the workpaper cannot be rebuilt.

risks: Draft overstates or softens a finding
Asset use data from sites is incomplete
research_questions: Is asset use data (hours, kilometres) available per truck and forklift?
How many audit actions stay open past their deadline today?
Does management read the current reports, and which parts?

role.altitude: From posting, checking and reporting by hand to owning the rules, tie-outs, tests and templates that check every entry and draft every report, and reviewing their exceptions.
reach: FP&A Analyst: baseline rolling forecast and variance commentary
Bookkeeper: duplicate and IBAN-change checks before payment
Payroll Specialist: pre-filing payroll tax checks
Controller: continuous control evidence and audit follow-up
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: costing of benefit changes
role.ceiling_note: Most gains are in data gathering, testing and drafting; advice, tax positions, fraud follow-up and contact with the tax office and auditors stay human. Dutch GAAP, Dutch VAT and payroll rules are untested by benchmarks, so review stays essential; roughly 40-50% of hours on these tasks can be freed.
skills_to_grow: Writing control tests and rules (SQL or Power Query on the AFAS extract)
Reviewing AI output for hidden assumptions
AVG/GDPR and works council rules for data use
role.ambitious_version: Two accountants run continuous controls over every payment, payroll run and agency invoice, deliver weekly site flash reports and rolling forecasts, and help cut days to close with fewer audit adjustments.
